This date, which should not be regarded as the true founding year, actually marks the reformation of the current entity following its bankruptcy in 1995. | stadium = [[Nouste Camp]] | capacity = 4,031 | owner = [[Bernard Laporte-Fray]] | chrtitle = President | chairman = Bernard Laporte-Fray | mgrtitle = Head coach | manager = [[Thierry Debès]] | league = {{French football updater|Pau}} | season = {{French football updater|Pau2}} | position = {{French football updater|Pau3}} | pattern_name1 = | pattern_la1 = _PauFC2425h | pattern_b1 = _PauFC2425h | pattern_ra1 = _PauFC2425h | pattern_sh1 = _PauFC2425h | pattern_so1 = _PauFC2425h | leftarm1 = | body1 = | rightarm1 = | shorts1 = | socks1 = | pattern_la2 = _PauFC2425a | pattern_b2 = _PauFC2425a | pattern_ra2 = _PauFC2425a | pattern_sh2 = _PauFC2425a | pattern_so2 = _jomafootballwhitelogo | leftarm2 = | body2 = | rightarm2 = | shorts2 = | socks2 = 073662 | pattern_la3 = | pattern_b3 = | pattern_ra3 = | pattern_sh3 = | pattern_so3 = | leftarm3 = | body3 = | rightarm3 = | shorts3 = | socks3 = | website = {{official URL}} | current = 2025–26 Pau FC season | coordinates = }} '''Pau Football Club''' ({{IPA|fr|po futbol klœb}}), commonly referred to as '''Pau FC''', is a professional [[Association football|football]] club based in [[Pau, Pyrénées-Atlantiques|Pau]], capital of [[Béarn]], France. Pau FC plays its home matches at the [[Nouste Camp]] and competes in [[Ligue 2]], the [[French football league system|second tier of French football]]. Nicknamed Les Maynats, Pau FC traces its origins to the [[Parochial patronage|patronage]] of the '''Bleuets de Notre-Dame''', officially founded in 1920 in the Mayolis district. By the onset of the 1958–59 season, the Bleuets had ascended to the highest amateur division in the [[French football league system]].{{Citation needed|date=January 2026}} Under the stewardship of its founding president, José Bidegain, the Bleuets de Notre-Dame's senior team transitioned into the '''Football-Club de Pau'''. By the 60s, they had settled in the [[Stade du Hameau]], harbouring ambitions of turning professional. Recurrent financial troubles weakened the club, necessitating interventions from the municipal authorities of Pau. The team later{{When|date=January 2026}}, dropped back to the regional South West League. The 90s witnessed reckless spending in pursuit of promotion to [[Ligue 2]], culminating in financial insolvency and relegation to the fourth tier of [[French football league system|French football]] in 1995.{{Citation needed|date=January 2026}} A revival came under the guidance of former players [[Bernard Laporte-Fray]] and [[Joël Lopez (footballer, born 1960)|Joël Lopez]], who rebranded the club as Pau Football Club. Financial restructuring ensued, stabilising the club in the third tier until [[2007–08 Championnat National|2007]]. However, subsequent relegation compounded by non-sporting crises, delayed their return to the third division until the [[2016–17 Championnat National|2016–17 season]]. In 2019, marking 59 years since its inception, Pau FC celebrated the opening of its inaugural stadium, [[Nouste Camp]]. The club's achievements include winning the [[Championnat National]] in 2020, winning the [[Championnat National 2|National 2]] title twice in 1998 and 2016 and winning the French South-West League in 1958 and 1968. The team claimed victory in the [[Championnat National]], the third division, during the [[2019–20 Championnat National|2019–20 season]], which promoted the club to [[Ligue 2]]. This ushered in a period of unprecedented success, as the club seeks to firmly establish itself in the realm of the [[French football league system]]."}}
